phase3_1_protocol_config._note: This file is the single source of truth for the Phase 3.1 evaluation protocol. It was written and committed BEFORE any Phase 3.1 result was produced. Do not edit values in this file to chase a better-looking result -- see docs/PHASE3_1_EVALUATION_PROTOCOL.md section 'Core Scientific Principle'.
phase3_1_protocol_config._regime_sizes_note: Unchanged from Phase 2 (src/pipeline_builder.DEFAULT_REGIME_SIZES). Regime 0 = train workload model, regime 1 = calibration/validation, regime 2 = failure-memory fit/validation, regimes 3+4 = untouched test.
phase3_1_protocol_config._n_clusters_note: Unchanged from Phase 2 default. Not tuned in Phase 3.1.
phase3_1_protocol_config._seeds_note: Predetermined before any Phase 3.1 run. 1-5 are a plain sequential convention; 42 is retained for continuity with the original Phase 2 single-seed result. No seed has been added or removed after inspecting results.
phase3_1_protocol_config._primary_seed_note: The seed used for the bootstrap-CI (within-seed sampling uncertainty) analysis, chosen because it is the original Phase 2 seed, not because it produces the most favorable numbers.
phase3_1_protocol_config._coverage_operating_points_note: Fixed fractions of the test set flagged as 'high risk', decided a priori. Precision/recall are reported at these coverage levels rather than at a score threshold chosen to maximize any test-set metric.
phase3_1_protocol_config.aurc_coverage_grid: 5%-100% in 5-point steps, inherited unchanged from benchmarks/risk_coverage.py (Phase 2, not modified in Phase 3.1)

bootstrap.method: nonparametric percentile bootstrap, resampling (y_true, y_score) rows with replacement

cross_seed_confidence_interval.method: Student-t interval over per-seed point estimates (n=6 seeds, too few for a normal approximation)

phase3_1_protocol_config.failure_definition: workload_model.predict(x).predicted_label != true_label, evaluated on regimes 3+4 (the held-out test stream) using the frozen (regime-0-trained) workload model

baselines.A_no_signal: constant score equal to the empirical failure prevalence measured on the regime-2 logging set (train-side data, never test)
baselines.C_failure_memory: FailureMemory.risk(context, confidence), Phase 2's unmodified KMeans/Gaussian-kernel similarity score

phase3_5_attack_protocol._note: Phase 3.5 attack-generalization protocol. Written and committed BEFORE any Phase 3.5 result was produced. Do not edit values in this file to chase a better-looking result -- see docs/PHASE3_5_ATTACK_GENERALIZATION.md section 'Scientific integrity'. Inherits, and does NOT override, configs/phase3_1_protocol.json's regime_sizes, n_clusters, seeds, primary_seed, coverage_operating_points, calibration_bins, bootstrap, and cross_seed_confidence_interval -- those are read directly from that file by benchmarks/phase3_5_attack_generalization.py, not duplicated here.
phase3_5_attack_protocol._seeds_note: Identical to the frozen Phase 3.1 seed list. No seed added or removed for Phase 3.5.

candidates.A_no_signal: Phase 3.1 baseline A, unchanged: constant score = empirical failure prevalence on regime 2 (train-side).
candidates.C_original_failure_memory: Phase 3.1 baseline C / Phase 3.2 control, unchanged: FailureMemory.risk(context, confidence), the unmodified Phase 2 KMeans/Gaussian-kernel similarity score.
candidates.D_supervised_failure_risk: Referred to as 'F' in Phase 3.4's naming. The exact Phase 3.2C Experiment B / Phase 3.3 frozen candidate: Phase2RepresentationSupervisedRisk (old Phase 2 PCA representation + logistic regression), fit once per seed on regime-2 clean data and reused unmodified across every condition.

phase3_5_attack_protocol._candidates_note: Internal key names in this file and in benchmarks/phase3_5_attack_generalization.py match benchmarks/phase3_3_generalization.py's BASELINES list verbatim (that module's functions are reused directly, not reimplemented). D_supervised_failure_risk is Phase 3.4's 'F'; the report and JSON output use the display label 'F' for continuity with Phase 3.4.
phase3_5_attack_protocol._primary_comparison_note: Calibrated confidence (B) is a co-equal baseline, not an already-surpassed one (Phase 3.4 status: INCONCLUSIVE). F is a candidate under investigation. D/E (Phase 3.2 raw-features / failure-history candidates) are NOT re-evaluated in Phase 3.5 -- out of scope per the brief's instruction to avoid unnecessary expansion.
phase3_5_attack_protocol.training_condition: Exactly build_system(regime_sizes, n_clusters, seed) at the generator's default drift_scale=0.35 -- regimes 0/1/2 CLEAN and unmodified, identical to Phase 3.1/3.2/3.2C/3.3. F is fit exactly once per seed via the unmodified Phase2RepresentationSupervisedRisk.fit() on regime-2 clean data (src.evaluation.representations, reused, not modified), reusing benchmarks.phase3_3_generalization's _reconstruct_regime2_with_confidences and _fit_frozen_candidate helpers verbatim. No attack condition is ever used for fitting.

clean_reference_condition.description: system.test_stream verbatim (regimes 3+4, drift_scale=0.35) -- byte-identical to Phase 3.1/3.2/3.2C/3.3's 'original_benchmark' condition. Not regenerated or modified.

attack_matrix.rationale: Additive N(0, 0.5^2) noise on every one of the 5 raw features (which are themselves N(0,1) by construction -- see src/data/synthetic.py), applied only to regime-3/4 context dicts AFTER generation. std=0.5 is half the native feature scale, chosen a priori as the 'mild' anchor before any evaluation was run. Represents corrupted/noisy telemetry reaching the deployed system: the true label-generating relationship (base_w, drift) is untouched, only what every candidate OBSERVES changes -- a covariate-shift attack, not concept drift.

Same mechanism as feature_noise_mild, std=1.5 (1.5x native feature scale), chosen a priori as the 'severe' anchor -- fixed before evaluation, not tuned to any outcome. Provides a dose-response comparison against feature_noise_mild.

attack_matrix.severity: n/a -- binary corruption, not a graded severity
attack_matrix.rationale: Zeroes features f2 and f4 (the 2nd and 4th of 5 features by the fixed FEATURE_NAMES order -- a systematic 'every other feature starting at index 1' rule stated here before evaluation, not chosen after inspecting which features matter most) for every regime-3/4 sample. Simulates a sensor/telemetry field going dark or being stripped -- a qualitatively different corruption (structural, not magnitude-graded) from the noise attacks. Fully deterministic, no RNG needed.

excluded_axes.concept_drift_boundary_rotation: Already covered by Phase 3.3's drift_scale sweep (weaker/stronger multiples of the training drift_scale); not repeated here to avoid re-running the same axis under a new name.
excluded_axes.label_boundary_manipulation: Would require either modifying src/data/synthetic.py's generate_regime_stream (the frozen shared generator used by every prior phase) or reimplementing its base_w/rng construction externally (risking a subtly inconsistent, undocumented reimplementation of the label-generating process). Neither is done in Phase 3.5. This is an explicit, documented limitation, not a fabricated attack.
excluded_axes.failure_rate_shift: The generator does not expose an independent failure-rate/prevalence control -- prevalence is an emergent property of X, base_w, and drift_scale. Cannot be varied in isolation without changing the meaning of the task or re-deriving the generator's internals; not attempted.

phase3_5_attack_protocol.fitting_rule: Every candidate is fit EXACTLY once per seed, on regime-0/1/2 CLEAN data, before any condition (clean or attacked) is scored. The fitted objects (workload_model, calibrator, failure_memory, the Phase2RepresentationSupervisedRisk candidate) are then reused UNMODIFIED to score the clean reference condition and every attack condition in turn. No .fit() call occurs anywhere in the attack-scoring path. No attack parameter, attack severity, or attack result is ever used to select, tune, retrain, or threshold any candidate.

robustness_metric.name: excess_auroc_retention_ratio
robustness_metric.definition: (attack_auroc - 0.5) / (clean_auroc - 0.5), computed per seed then aggregated across seeds via the same Student-t interval used for every other cross-seed metric. Defined here, before any Phase 3.5 result was computed, specifically for AUROC, whose uninformative floor (0.5, random ranking) makes a raw ratio (attack_auroc / clean_auroc) misleading. Undefined (reported as null, not fabricated) when clean_auroc == 0.5 (no informative signal to retain in the first place, applies to A_no_signal by construction).
robustness_metric.also_reported: Absolute AUROC/AUPRC/AURC/precision@coverage/recall@coverage degradation (clean metric - attack metric) for every candidate and condition -- no ratio needed for these, reported directly.

phase3_5_attack_protocol.no_new_hyperparameter_tuning: No candidate's hyperparameters, feature representation, calibration, PCA dimensionality, KMeans configuration, or fitting procedure is changed in Phase 3.5 relative to Phase 3.2C Experiment B / Phase 3.3. If a candidate performs poorly under an attack condition, that is reported as a result, not corrected.

complementarity_subexperiment.reason: Out of Phase 3.5's core objective (attack generalization). Documented per the brief as a REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP GATE before any autonomous integration of Failure Risk -- not attempted here, to avoid silently redefining Phase 3.5's scope.

display_labels.D_supervised_failure_risk: F -- Supervised Failure Risk (Phase 3.2C Experiment B / Phase 3.3 frozen candidate)

meta.note: Phase 3.1 protocol reused unmodified. F is the exact Phase 3.2C Experiment B / Phase 3.3 frozen candidate, fit once per seed on clean regime-2 data and reused unmodified across the clean reference condition and every attack condition. No refitting on any condition.
